meta.title: Florida Voting Documents Tool
meta.description: Find out what documents you may need to vote in Florida under HB991 (the 2026 documentary proof of citizenship law).

q_has_fl_id.text: Do you have a Florida driver's license or state ID card?

q_real_id.text: Does your Florida license or ID have a gold star in the upper right corner?
q_real_id.hint: The gold star indicates a REAL ID.

q_naturalized_before_id.text: Are you a naturalized U.S. citizen who obtained your Florida driver's license or ID before becoming a U.S. citizen?

result_naturalized_pre_id.heading: Update your DHSMV record.
result_naturalized_pre_id.body: A law passed in 2025 requires all naturalized citizens to update their Florida DL/ID record to include documentation of their naturalization. Use the link below to learn how. When updating your DL/ID record, be sure to select the option to update your voter registration as well — that way the necessary evidence of citizenship is reflected in your voter file.

links.label: DHSMV — updating your record after naturalization (TODO: confirm URL)

signup.heading: Want help with this?
signup.body: Sign up and Common Cause will send guidance.

q_used_id_to_register.text: Did you use your Florida driver's license or ID when you registered to vote?

result_real_id_registered.heading: You're most likely all set.
result_real_id_registered.body: Your voter record most likely already contains the necessary evidence of citizenship and you should not have to take any additional steps. We recommend you check your registration to make sure your name and address are up to date.

signup.heading: Stay informed.
signup.body: Sign up for updates from Common Cause on Florida voting rights.

result_real_id_not_registered.heading: Update your voter record to include your Florida DL/ID number.
result_real_id_not_registered.body: You can do this in any of four ways: (1) call your county Supervisor of Elections, (2) go to RegisterToVoteFlorida.gov and request a new voter information card (enter your FL DL/ID number when requesting), (3) submit a paper voter registration application, or (4) visit a county SOE office. You should also make sure your name and address are up to date.

q_willing_real_id.text: Are you willing and able to get a Florida REAL ID driver's license or ID?

result_get_real_id.heading: Start the process of getting a REAL ID.
result_get_real_id.body: We recommend you begin the process of obtaining an updated FL DL/ID from the DHSMV. When you are offered the option to register to vote or update your voter registration record, select "yes" — the necessary evidence of citizenship will then be reflected in your voter file.

links.label: DHSMV — how to get a REAL ID (TODO: confirm URL)

signup.heading: Want help?
signup.body: Sign up and Common Cause will walk you through it.

result_check_real_id_eligibility.heading: Check whether you can get a REAL ID, then come back.
result_check_real_id_eligibility.body: Use the link below to see if you're able to get a Florida REAL ID, then come back here and choose the option that best fits your situation. If you need help obtaining a FL DL/ID, contact Vote Riders.

q_has_citizenship_docs.text: Do you have any of the following documents?

choices.label: Original or certified copy of birth certificate

result_passport_meets.heading: Your passport meets the citizenship requirement.
result_passport_meets.body: You may be contacted by your county Supervisor of Elections requesting evidence of your citizenship. If you are, your valid passport meets the requirement. Check your registration to make sure your name and address are up to date. Respond promptly to any mail from your county SOE — and if you receive mail and are uncertain whether it's authentic, call your county SOE.

signup.heading: Stay informed.
signup.body: Sign up for updates from Common Cause.

q_name_matches_birth_cert.text: Is your current legal name the same as the name on your birth certificate?

result_birth_cert_meets.heading: Your birth certificate meets the citizenship requirement.
result_birth_cert_meets.body: You may be contacted by your county Supervisor of Elections requesting evidence of your citizenship. If you are, your birth certificate should meet the requirement. Check your registration to make sure your name and address are up to date, and respond promptly to any mail from your county SOE.

result_birth_cert_name_change.heading: You'll need your birth certificate plus name-change documentation.
result_birth_cert_name_change.body: If your county Supervisor of Elections contacts you requesting evidence of your citizenship, you'll need to provide your birth certificate AND documentation linking your current name to the name on your birth certificate. This can include original or certified copies of marriage certificate(s), divorce decree(s), or court order. If you don't have these documents, the links below can help you obtain replacements. If you need assistance, contact Vote Riders.

signup.heading: We can help you gather what you need.
signup.body: Sign up and Common Cause will send guidance.

result_naturalization_meets.heading: Your naturalization certificate meets the citizenship requirement.
result_naturalization_meets.body: You may be contacted by your county Supervisor of Elections requesting evidence of your citizenship. If you are, your naturalization certificate should meet the requirement. Check your registration to make sure your name and address are up to date, and respond promptly to any mail from your county SOE.

result_naturalization_name_change.heading: You'll need your naturalization certificate plus name-change documentation.
result_naturalization_name_change.body: If your county Supervisor of Elections contacts you requesting evidence of your citizenship, you'll need to provide your naturalization certificate AND documentation linking your current name to the name on the certificate. This can include marriage certificate(s), divorce decree(s), or court order. If you don't have these documents, the links below can help you obtain replacements. For assistance, contact Vote Riders.

result_obtain_birth_cert_us.heading: Obtain a copy of your birth certificate.
result_obtain_birth_cert_us.body: If your county Supervisor of Elections contacts you requesting evidence of your citizenship, your birth certificate should meet the requirement. Use the links below to obtain a copy, depending on the state you were born in. For assistance, contact Vote Riders.

result_obtain_birth_cert_us_name.heading: Obtain your birth certificate and name-change documentation.
result_obtain_birth_cert_us_name.body: If your county Supervisor of Elections contacts you requesting evidence of your citizenship, you'll need to provide your birth certificate AND documentation linking your current name to your name at birth. This can include marriage certificate(s), divorce decree(s), or court order. Use the links below to obtain copies. For assistance, contact Vote Riders.

result_derived_citizen.heading: Under construction — derived citizenship guidance.
result_derived_citizen.body: This branch is still being filled in by Florida program staff. Derived citizens (people who became U.S. citizens because a parent naturalized before they turned 18) often do not have a naturalization certificate of their own. Common Cause Florida is determining what documentation works in this case and what replacement options exist. Check back soon.

result_no_fl_id.heading: Under construction — guidance for voters without a Florida ID.
result_no_fl_id.body: This branch is still being filled in. If you don't have a Florida driver's license or state ID, you may still be able to register and vote, but the path forward depends on what other documents you have and whether you're able to obtain a Florida ID. Common Cause Florida is finalizing the guidance for this case. Check back soon.
